# Further Reading {#sec-further-reading}

This is a route into primary guidance, not a list to memorise. Consult the
source for the decision you are making. Standards, product behaviour and
legal requirements can change; these links were selected in September 2026.

## Foundations, identity and cryptography

The [NIST Cybersecurity Framework](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework) organises
outcomes and governance. [ASD's Essential Eight](https://www.cyber.gov.au/business-government/asds-cyber-security-frameworks/essential-eight)
provides a different resource: mitigation strategies and maturity guidance.
Neither removes the need to understand the organisation's risks.

[NIST SP 800-63B-4](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-4/sp800-63b.html) distinguishes
authenticators, password verifiers, recovery and sessions.
[OWASP's password-storage guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html)
explains implementation choices. Read these when assessing a login design,
rather than implementing a password store from a textbook sketch.

[FIPS 186-5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final) covers digital signatures;
[TLS 1.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446.html) shows authentication,
key establishment and traffic protection as separate operations.
They are references for checking explanations, not prerequisites for the
paper exercises.

## Software, networks and incidents

The [CVE programme](https://www.cve.org/ResourcesSupport/FAQs),
[CWE catalogue](https://cwe.mitre.org/) and
[CERT/CC disclosure guide](https://vuls.cert.org/confluence/display/CVD)
help distinguish a vulnerability record, a recurring weakness and the
process of coordinating disclosure.

[OWASP's access-control guidance](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/)
and [XSS prevention guidance](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html)
expand the web chapter. [Wireshark's Ethernet capture guidance](https://wiki.wireshark.org/capturesetup/Ethernet)
helps explain the limits of an observation point.

[NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/61/r3/final)
connects incident response to risk management.
[CISA's ransomware guide](https://www.cisa.gov/stopransomware/ransomware-guide)
includes preparation, data theft and recovery.
[NIST's contingency-planning resource](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework/nist-sp-800-34)
supports recovery objectives and testing.

## Legal decisions and historical evidence

[OAIC's NDB guidance](https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/notifiable-data-breaches/preventing-preparing-for-and-responding-to-data-breaches/data-breach-preparation-and-response/part-4-notifiable-data-breach-ndb-scheme)
and [EDPB's GDPR notification guidance](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/documents/guideline/guidelines-92022-on-personal-data-breach-notification-under-gdpr_en)
describe different regimes. Coverage, facts, recipients and thresholds
matter. Use authorised advice for a real incident.

The [Senate staff report on Target](https://www.commerce.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/media/doc/2014%200325%20Target%20Kill%20Chain%20Analysis.pdf)
is an analysis of reporting available in 2014. Treat its proposed
interventions as possible opportunities, not proven counterfactuals.
The chapter on cybercrime links the investigating agencies' accounts of
Gameover Zeus and Mirai.

The [NCSC assessment of AI threats to 2027](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/report/impact-ai-cyber-threat-now-2027)
is a dated assessment. Separate observed capability, forecast and your own
inference when using it.

## Learning beyond the book

The [practice appendix](lab-environment.qmd) explains the scope and safety
checks for optional technical work. [Incident Zero](https://incidentzero.retroverse.studio/)
offers group practice. Its materials have their own licence; this book
links them without incorporating them.

For the next security-track step, see
[*Substantiate, Don't Assume*](https://michael-borck.github.io/substantiate-dont-assume/).
For learning conversations, see
[*Conversation, Not Delegation*](https://michael-borck.github.io/conversation-not-delegation/).
Both are optional: the [dossier](defender-dossier.qmd) is self-contained.
